IndusEquip Corporation - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the IndusEquip Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss IndusEquip Corporation's results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and David Kim, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on IndusEquip Corporation's performance for the third quarter of 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, navigating a choppy macro environment with resilience and executing against our strategic priorities. Key highlights include delivering strong organic revenue growth complemented by smart inorganic contributions from recent acquisitions, robust order intake and favorable book-to-bill trends across core end markets like construction, mining, and agriculture, accelerated expansion in our automation and digital offerings that's enhancing efficiency for both customers and our operations, meaningful cost reduction efforts driving margin expansion, and a positive outlook for end-market growth in the near and medium term as secular trends like electrification and reshoring take hold.

Our $4.2 billion backlog, up 20% year-over-year, with book-to-bill at 1.25 times, gives us excellent visibility, and we're confident these initiatives are positioning us for sustained growth ahead.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, John. Good afternoon, everyone. Let's dive into our financial performance. For the third quarter, IndusEquip reported consolidated revenue of $2.85 billion, up 14% year-over-year on a reported basis and 13% at constant currency. This reflects the strength of our core industrial equipment business amid softening industrial capex in some areas, offset by strong demand in automation and electrification.

Starting with organic revenue growth, we achieved a solid 9% year-over-year, or 10% excluding a $25 million foreign exchange headwind from a stronger U.S. dollar against the euro and Chinese yuan. This is our sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit constant-currency organic growth, accelerating from 8% in the prior year and surpassing the peer average of around 6%, according to ISI Evercore data. Pricing drove 4 points, with mid-single-digit increases on heavy earthmoving gear like our E-Series hydraulic excavators and PrecisionMach CNC milling centers. Premium lines with IoT and predictive maintenance, such as SmartLift AGVs, realized 7-9% premiums due to clear ROI in labor-constrained settings. Volumes contributed 5 points, led by a manufacturing capex recovery, with our Automation & Robotics segment up 15% organically from cobot bookings tied to the Nexus AI platform, echoing trends at Fanuc and ABB. Automotive reshoring, including a $150 million run-rate with a Detroit Three OEM for welding lines, and 12% growth in Aerospace & Defense from F-35 tooling, were standouts.

Regionally, North America led at 12% organic, boosted by IIJA funding for data centers and EV gigafactories—our Surface Mining division grew 18% on haul trucks for lithium ops. EMEA hit 7%, helped by wind turbine gearless drivetrains despite energy destocking. Asia-Pacific was flat at 1% due to China's property slowdown impacting excavators and cranes, but offset by 20% growth in semiconductor fab equipment for TSMC's U.S. sites.

Inorganically, acquisitions added 4 points or $115 million, primarily from our $450 million July purchase of RoboForge Technologies, a precision laser welding leader for EV batteries, contributing $85 million—75% of its TTM run-rate—and surpassing $50 million synergy goals via cross-selling motion control software. Precision Dynamics, acquired for $120 million in May for aerospace spindles, added $30 million, ramping quickly through shared channels. Together, they've lifted automation to 28% of mix from 22%, added 150 basis points to EBITDA via $20 million in procurement and facility synergies, and expanded our high-growth adjacencies.

This blend validates our buy-and-build-plus-innovate approach, with over 5% of sales reinvested in Industry 4.0 digital twins and hybrid-electric drivetrains to capture sustainability tailwinds like EU CBAM and U.S. IRA incentives. We expect Q4 organic at 8-10%, inorganic at 5 points, full-year organic at 9.5%, and total growth of 12-14%.

Gross margin reached 32.4%, up 410 basis points year-over-year, driven by these dynamics and cost discipline. Operating expenses were $520 million, yielding operating income of $312 million. Net income came in at $210 million, or $1.42 per share.

Turning to our automation and digital offerings, this segment generated $285 million, up 28% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, now 32% of total revenue—up 5 points—and with recurring ACV up 42% to $1.2 billion from multi-year contracts. Amid labor shortages and sustainability pushes, we're seeing retrofits of legacy equipment with modular kits at record pace, outpacing the 9-11% market CAGR. Our IndusEdge platform, using ML on 50 petabytes of data, predicts hydraulic or servo failures 72 hours ahead at 92% accuracy, boosting customer OEE by 12-18% and cutting downtime 15-25%. A tier-1 auto supplier saw 22% throughput gains, 30% energy savings on EV lines, with payback under 14 months and 68% segment margins.

North America grew 32%, Europe 25% via Green Deal subsidies, APAC 38% from China 2025 and India PLI. We're investing $450 million in R&D, including an Atlanta AI center with NVIDIA, shifting to 60% as-a-service models for 22% EBITDA margins by 2026. Internally, it's cut our scrap 14% and maintenance 21%, adding 150 bps to margins. FY25 segment growth targeted at 25-30%, rACV to $1.8 billion.

Cost reduction has been pivotal, delivering $178 million in YTD run-rate savings against a $2.1 billion COGS base—an 8.5% cut ahead of our 6% goal. Supply chain optimization (45% of savings) via Forge Forward consolidated suppliers to 850, yielding 7-9% on materials; nearshoring 25% of Asia components to Mexico cut logistics 15%, Poland localization saved €12 million. Manufacturing productivity (30%) deployed 450 cobots, AI maintenance slashed downtime 28%, VFDs cut energy 22%, lifting labor output 17%. Overhead discipline (15%) via zero-based budgeting trimmed SG&A to 9.9%, cloud ERP sped procurement 40%. Hedging and sustainability (10%) locked steel at $650/ton, renewables qualified $5 million subsidies.

This expanded EBITDA to $312 million, margins to 18.2%—above industry 15.8%—FCF to $245 million up 35%, ROIC to 14.2%. 70% permanent, $220 million run-rate by year-end. Savings fund R&D for green tech.

On orders, intake was $1.42 billion, up 12% YoY, backlog $4.8 billion up 18%, book-to-bill 1.25x. Construction (42%) at $595 million up 22%, 1.35x ratio, led by NA IIJA projects, India pipeline, electrified gear at 18%. Mining (28%) $400 million up 9%, 1.28x, APAC nickel/iron ore, autonomous trucks. Ag (18%) $255 million down 5%, 1.05x from commodity softness, countered by autonomous sprayers. Oil/gas up 14%, power gen 10%.

For outlook, end markets grow 4-6% in 2024, 6-8% 2025 globally. Semis 12-15% near-term, factory auto 7-9%, construction/mining 3-5% rising to 5-7%, ag flat to 2% then 4-6%. NA 7-9%, Europe 3-5%, APAC 4-6%. Medium-term 7-9% CAGR to 2028 on electrification (40-50% hybrids), automation ($300B capex), reshoring. FY revenue $8.2-8.5 billion up 10-13%, EPS $6.80-7.20.

Operating margin guidance: Q4 at 18.5-19.5%, full-year 18.2-18.8%, benefiting from pricing, mix, efficiencies.

We're managing capital allocation sharply—high-growth investments, $150 million buybacks, 12% dividend hike.

Next, I will hand over to Lisa Patel, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've prioritized productivity and efficiency across our global manufacturing footprint. Lean principles and data analytics have optimized processes, while new tech bolsters supply chain resilience—95% on-time delivery despite rare earth lead times. We've expanded capacity 15% in key plants like Peoria and Monterrey, supporting backlog conversion at 85-90%. Workforce initiatives, including upskilling for automation, address labor gaps, with cobot deployments yielding 17% productivity gains.

And I would like to turn the call over to our CTO, David Kim, for an update on our technology roadmap.

David Kim (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We're driving innovation with heavy R&D in AI, machine learning, and IoT—over 5% of sales. Our new Nexus AI-integrated cobots and IndusEdge digital twins show early promise, reducing customer downtime 20-30% and enabling real-time factory simulations. Partnerships with NVIDIA and Siemens advance generative AI for edge optimization. The RoboForge integration accelerates laser welding for EVs, and we're targeting hydrogen compressors and e-axles. These will reshape industrial ops, with automation CAGR at 12% through 2028, creating big opportunities for IndusEquip.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the growth drivers in your digital solutions business?

David Kim:
Thanks, Alex. Absolutely—the digital solutions are firing on all cylinders, as Michael noted with the 28% segment growth and rACV surge to $1.2 billion. Key drivers include labor shortages pushing retrofits, where our IndusEdge platform's 92% predictive accuracy delivers 12-18% OEE lifts. Automotive EV lines are a hotspot, with 22% throughput gains for tier-1s, and regional momentum in APAC at 38% from fab and textile automation. Our as-a-service shift to 60% of contracts builds recurring streams, and internal use has cut our costs 21%. We're on track for 25-30% growth next year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen (Goldman Sachs):
What are your plans for expanding your presence in emerging markets?

John Reynolds:
Great question, Emily. Emerging markets, especially APAC and LATAM, are core to our growth, with India and Mexico as priorities. India's PLI and $1.3 trillion infra pipeline drove 35% construction orders; we're targeting 20% share in semis via Tata/Foxconn ties. Mexico's maquiladoras ramp via Monterrey at 50% capacity for Cummins/Tesla, aided by USMCA. Challenges like China slowdowns are offset by localization—25% nearshoring—and $200 million R&D for region-specific electrification. Expect 10-12% growth there medium-term on reshoring.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel (Morgan Stanley):
How are you addressing the skilled labor shortage in the manufacturing sector?

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, Raj. The 4.5% U.S. vacancy rate is industry-wide, but we're ahead with workforce development—training 5,000 associates in AI and cobots this year, partnerships with community colleges, and incentives for certifications. Operationally, 450 cobots automate 35% of welding/assembly, boosting productivity 17% and offsetting 5.2% wage inflation. Digital twins predict needs, and our as-a-service models attract talent via innovation. Retention is up 15%, positioning us strongly.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

John Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in IndusEquip. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
